issues.description: The algorithm only tries incrementing a single element by up to k-1 and checks if that alone makes the product divisible by k. This is logically incomplete: the minimum solution may require increments distributed across multiple elements (or multiple increments on the same element beyond a single try-upto-k-1 model depending on factorization reasoning). Thus the implementation can produce wrong results for cases that need multiple-element adjustments.

The implementation recomputes the entire product for every candidate increment by iterating over the whole array, nested in loops over indices and ops, yielding O(k * n^2) work per test case. With constraints sum n ≤ 2·10^5 this will TLE / be infeasible in realistic inputs.

If no single-element increment produces divisibility, min_operations returns float('inf'), which will be printed as "inf" instead of a valid integer. This reveals an uncovered return path leading to invalid output.
No unit tests or example-based test harness were provided in the workspace. The task required fixing an observed failing case (CA-02); no automated tests were added to prevent regressions.

The solution uses an explicit brute-force simulation (mutating and restoring the array while repeatedly computing product modulo k). A more maintainable and efficient approach is to work with counts / modular residues and aggregated product modulo k (or factor exponents for k=2..5) without O(n^2) recomputation.
